Great Food
Sep 2025 • Couples
Banh Mi Sandwich was a great meal. The owners use rice flour to make their world famous French style baguettes. The sandwich consists of pork, chicken or ham, with various vegetables and condiments. The sandwich dates back to about 1954 when Vietnam gained its independence from France. After the fall of Saigon in 1975 many refugees to the USA and Europe brought this recipe with them and is available in many Vietnamese restaurants around the world.

Best bánh mì ốp la!
Jan 2025 • Family
If you’re in Saigon and looking for an authentic Vietnamese breakfast experience, Bánh Mì Hòa Mã is a must-visit! This hidden gem serves up a delicious take on the classic bánh mì ốp la (baguette with eggs), complete with sizzling skillets of fried eggs, assorted meats, and pâté. The baguette is fresh and crispy, perfect for dipping into the rich yolk and savory sauces.

Service is quick, the food is flavorful, and the experience is unforgettable. Highly recommend visiting early to avoid the crowds. Definitely one of the best breakfast spots in the city!

Great Breakfast on the Street
Dec 2022
Walked here from our District 1 hotel and it was worth it. This is right on a busy street so you are sitting on a busy pavement with traffic going by. Motorbikes constantly stop for locals to pick up take-away. Foreigners like us were made very welcome, immediately seated and shown a menu which featured the "cooked breakfast" banh-mi we had gone for. The thing is that you may be eating fried processed pork (well what else is a sausage anywhere I suppose?) but the quality of bread, the pickles on the side, the iced very strong sweet Vietnamese coffee and the freshly cooked eggs just make this all totally delicious. Will definitely return next time in HCMC.

Amazing Bahn Mi Place
Feb 2020
This is street food at its best. Apparently on of the oldest bahn mi places in Saigon - it's been in business since 1958 continuously through the war, the difficult transition period from 1975 to1986 and now in the new Vietnam. There are just two choices on the menu - "traditional" bahn mi sandwich and a skillet bahn mi with egg, meat and more. Both are cheap (a little over $2 at most) and delicious. Others have described how busy it is and how efficiently they manage. Everything is fresh and clean. Amazing place. Don't miss it.

"MF LFF FIF FAFE!" (me with my mouth stuffed with Viet goodness...)
Oct 2019
Any travel blog you visit will tell you about this place and they're all spot on. It's definitely a must-eat destination in HCM. Crowded low tables straddle a side alley and scooters passing mere inches away spice your food w/ their exhaust, but oh what a taste to behold! Breakfast is served until the kitchen runs out (which is a daily occurrence) so come early to avoid the local rush. It's definitely a one-of-a-kind al fresco dining experience you won't forget soon.
